en: In order to build a web server with Deno, we
of course have to ensure that we are all on
the same page and we understand how the web
works. So here is how it works. Using the
web, if we simplify it, is just the
interaction of 2 parties.
We got the client, the user, so maybe you,
who might be using a browser or maybe also a
mobile app, does not matter. So some tool on
the client side, so on your local computer,
for example, to then reach out to a web
server.
Such a web server could host a website, so
it could contain multiple HTML files which
are
served to the clients,
or it just serves data and the client,
because it's maybe a mobile app, already
knows what to render on the screen and just
needs some data to, well, fill the screen
which is already rendering with some life.
That is how the web basically works.
Therefore, the server side, which is on a
different machine somewhere out there in the
world,
hosts the so-called backend code. So the
code which runs on that server, not on the
client side. And that typically is code that
reads or writes files, that interacts with a
database to store or fetch data Things like
that.
Now that server can be built and powered by
Deno.
So we will use Deno to build such a server
to which clients can send so-called
requests.
A request could be that I want to get an
HTML document which I, the browser let's
say, can render on the screen.
Or if the user is using a mobile app, this
mobile app could send a request for some
extra data which it wants to display on the
screen.
Now, of course, in order to show something
on the screen, which it is all about in the
end, sending a request is not enough. The
server also needs to send back a so-called
response.
And that is what we're going to build here.
We're going to build a Deno server that is
able to handle incoming requests and which
will then also send back responses.
